notes: Short: product team (5 engineers + 2 ML infra) evaluating move from hosted -> dedicated for predictable throughput.
Quote from CTO on 3/9: 'We need predictable p95 under load and a clear rollback story before committing to reserved capacity.'
Primary motivator: reduce per-token cost for high-volume reranking/embeddings while keeping latency SLAs for chat front-end.
Cost sensitivity: moderate-high. Will trade some model size for quantization if quality delta is small.
Security: must run in customer VPC, KMS for keys, retention policy 90 days, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM.
Current infra: GCP us-east1 primary; product traffic spikes during 9–11am PST; expectation ~120-180 req/s for chat endpoint during peak.
They asked for explicit region failover plan: us-east1 -> us-west2 -> eu-west1 (for disaster scenarios).
They requested a canary strategy that supports model variant fallback and automatic rollback on error/latency regressions.
Raised concern: model drift detection + eval hooks during canary (need lightweight eval set and automated regression alerting).
Decision criteria: p95 latency <= 300ms for chat (dedicated POC target), reranking throughput >= 150 qps, quality delta <= 2% measured by holdout prompts.
poc_plan: Duration: 4 weeks (2 weeks canary + ramp + 2 weeks soak + runbook verification)
Week 0 (prep): grant VPC peering + KMS key access; mount logs to their SIEM; confirm billing for POC pool
Canary: route 5% traffic to Dedicated pool (canary) for first 48 hours; run golden prompts and compare outputs vs hosted baseline
Model variants in canary: 'redwood-small-quant' (4-bit quantized) and 'redwood-medium-fp16' (higher quality) - auto-compare quality and latency
Fallback routing: if canary model fails health checks, route to hosted_api fallback; if region fails, route to secondary Dedicated region (us-west2), then hosted_api as last resort
Routing policy: prefer dedicated by tag (latency-cost tradeoff); fallback chain defined per route; automatic rollback if error rate >1.5% or p95 latency increases >35% vs baseline
Monitoring: P90/P95 latency, error rate, token cost per request, output similarity on eval set, and 'no downstream regressions' (customer-defined smoke tests)
Rollback: automated rollback playbook + manual abort path; SE-run drill on week 2 to test rollback and failover
Success criteria: sustained p95 <= 300ms, reranking throughput >=150 qps, cost/unit improvement >=20% vs hosted baseline, no critical security blocker
Deliverables: POC report (latency/cost/quality), runbook, recommended Dedicated pool sizing and canary configuration
